exposure: Type of surgery (general surgery, obstetric cases, Caesarean section, total abdominal hysterectomy, bowel resection and primary anastomosis, perforated peptic ulcer repair)
cohort: A hospital-based cross-sectional study of 181 patients (62.4% female, median age 39 years) referred to Muhimbili National Hospital in Tanzania for further management of postoperative complications.
finding: Surgical Site Infection (SSI) was the most common postoperative complication (52%), followed by gastrointestinal complications (31%), but none of the investigated factors were found to have a statistically significant association with SSI.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was one of the surgical procedures analyzed (24.9% of patients), but it was not found to have a statistically significant association with Surgical Site Infection (SSI).
